'''Stephen George Simpson''' (born September 8, 1945) is an American mathematician whose research concerns the [[foundations of mathematics]], including work in [[mathematical logic]], [[recursion theory]], and [[Ramsey theory]]. He is known for his extensive development of the field of [[reverse mathematics]] founded by [[Harvey Friedman (mathematician)|Harvey Friedman]], in which the goal is to determine which axioms are needed to prove certain mathematical theorems.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Elwes | first = Richard
 | isbn = 978-1-62365-054-4
 | mr = 3222699
 | page = 397
 | publisher = Quercus, New York
 | title = Math in 100 key breakthroughs
 | url = http://www.personal.psu.edu/t20/Elwes.pdf
 | year = 2013}}.</ref> He has also argued for the benefits of [[Finitism|finitistic]] mathematical systems, such as [[primitive recursive arithmetic]], which do not include [[actual infinity]].<ref>{{citation|title=Dispute over infinity divides mathematicians|first=Natalie|last=Wolchover|magazine=[[Scientific American]]|date=December 6, 2013|url=http://www.personal.psu.edu/t20/131203-Scientific-American.pdf}}.</ref>

A conference in honor of Simpson's 70th birthday was organized in May 2016.<ref>{{citation|title=The Foundational Impact of Recursion Theory: In honor of Steve Simpson's 70th birthday|work=Mathematics |url=http://www.marshall.edu/math/FIRT16/|date=May 22, 2016|accessdate=2016-05-06}}.</ref>

==Education==
Simpson graduated in 1966 from [[Lehigh University]] with a B.A. (summa cum laude) and M.A. in mathematics.<ref name="cv">{{citation|title=Curriculum vitae|first=Stephen G.|last=Simpson|date=January 21, 2016|url=http://www.personal.psu.edu/t20/papers/cv.pdf|accessdate=2016-05-06}}</ref> He earned a Ph.D. from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1971, with a dissertation entitled ''Admissible Ordinals and Recursion Theory'' and supervised by [[Gerald Sacks]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=22617}}</ref>

==Career==
After short-term positions at [[Yale University]], the [[University of California, Berkeley]], and the [[University of Oxford]], Simpson became an assistant professor at the [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 1975. At Penn State, he was Raymond N. Shibley professor from 1987 to 1992.<ref name="cv"/>

In 2016, his wife, computer scientist [[Padma Raghavan]], moved from Penn State to [[Vanderbilt University]] to become vice provost for research,<ref>{{citation|title=Vanderbilt names Padma Raghavan as vice provost for research|first=Melanie|last=Moran|url=http://news.vanderbilt.edu/2015/12/vanderbilt-names-padma-raghavan-vice-provost-for-research/|magazine=Research news @ Vanderbilt|publisher=Vanderbilt University|date=December 2015|accessdate=2016-05-06}}.</ref> and Simpson followed her, becoming a [[research professor]] at Vanderbilt.<ref>{{citation|title=Faculty profile|url=http://as.vanderbilt.edu/math/bio/stephen-simpson|publisher=[[Vanderbilt University]]|accessdate=2016-05-06}}.</ref>
